title: Metabolic enzymes of human SGBS adipocytes interact with halogenated bisphenol A alternatives – TPP Data
projectDescription: This dataset contains mass spectrometry–based thermal proteome profiling data. The assay was performed using lysates from differentiated human SGBS adipocytes. Cells were lysed, and protein concentrations were normalized prior to incubation with bisphenols, rosiglitazone, or vehicle control, followed by application of a temperature gradient to assess compound-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Soluble protein fractions were processed using SP3 bead–based cleanup, reduced, alkylated, and digested with trypsin. Peptides were labeled with tandem mass tags (TMT) to enable multiplexed quantitative analysis.  Mass spectrometry data were analyzed using the R package TPP, including normalization, melting curve fitting, and determination of protein melting temperatures. Compound-induced thermal stability shifts were identified based on statistically significant melting point differences and stringent quality control criteria to ensure reproducibility and reliability of candidate targets.
sampleProcessingProtocol: SGBS cells were cultured in 150 mm dishes and differentiated until day 12 of adipogenesis. Cells were harvested, lysed, and protein lysates were cleared of cellular debris and lipids by centrifugation. Protein concentrations were determined, and samples were normalized to equal concentrations. Lysates were incubated in quadruplicate with 10 µM bisphenols or rosiglitazone, while DMSO served as the vehicle control. Thermal proteome profiling was performed by exposing the samples to a defined temperature gradient to induce temperature-dependent protein denaturation. Following centrifugation, the soluble, non-denatured protein fractions were collected for downstream analysis. Protein samples were prepared using Sera-Mag SP3 magnetic beads for protein cleanup and digestion. Equal amounts of protein were reduced, alkylated, and bound to the beads in the presence of acetonitrile. Bead-bound proteins were washed to remove contaminants and digested overnight with trypsin. Resulting peptides were labelled with tandem mass tags (TMT) at a defined label-to-protein ratio, and the labelling reaction was quenched prior to sample pooling according to temperature conditions within each replicate. Peptides were subsequently washed, eluted from the beads, vacuum-dried, reconstituted in water, acidified with formic acid, and transferred to MS vials for downstream mass spectrometry analysis.  Samples were loaded into the autosampler of an LC-MS/MS system consisting of a nano high-performance liquid chromatography setup (Ultimate 3000 RSL Cnano, Dionex, Thermo Fisher Scientific), coupled via a TriVersa NanoMate (Advion, Ithaca, NY, USA) operating in LC chip coupling mode to a Q Exactive™ HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). A total of 5 µL per sample was injected and initially concentrated on a reverse-phase trapping column (Acclaim PepMap 100 C18, 2 µm, 75 µm × 5 cm, nanoViper, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using 4% mobile phase B (80% acetonitrile in nanopure water with 0.08% formic acid) and 96% mobile phase A (nanopure water with 0.1% formic acid) at a flow rate of 0.3 µL/min. Subsequently, peptides were separated on an analytical reverse-phase column (Acclaim PepMap 100 C18, nanoViper, 3 µm, 75 µm × 25 cm, Thermo Fisher Scientific). Elution was performed over a 180-minute two-step gradient ranging from 4% to 50% mobile phase B. The separated peptides were analyzed on the Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer at a resolution of 120,000 within a scan range of 350–1,550 m/z. The top 15 most intense precursor ions were selected for MS/MS fragmentation using a quadrupole with an isolation window of 0.7 m/z and acquired at a resolution of 60,000. Dynamic exclusion was set to 45 seconds.
dataProcessingProtocol: The MS raw files were processed using ProteomeDiscoverer (2.5.0.400) and the database search was performed using the UniprotKB/Swissprot reference proteome of Homo sapiens (17 July 2023). The resulting abundances were used for further data analysis and candidate selection.
